tags.name: Plaza la Isla. Atardecer al lado del muelle
Selina Hotel Cancun Lagoon Zona Hotelera

tags.addr:housenumber: "Novo Cancún Torre 1” Mz 27 Lt 1-02 UC-20 UP-P Secc.
tags.name: SLS Cancun Hotel & Residences
La Villa du Golf à Cancún
Dreams Vista Cancún Golf & Spa Resort

voyage.name: Interactive Aquarium
voyage.price: US$15 basic admissions (2022), more to swim with dolphins and other activities
voyage.content: In the middle of the La Isla Shopping Village in the hotel zone, this small, modern aquarium lets you get up close and personal with aquatic life. You can pet rays, nurse sharks, touch starfish, etc. You can pay to swim with captive dolphins in a large pool. There's a Mexican/seafood restaurant above the aquarium, where you can watch dolphin shows (or dolphins playing amongst themselves in between shows) while eating

voyage.name: El Rey Archaeological Zone
voyage.content: Small Maya archaeological site on the south end of the hotel zone. The settlement was at its peak around 250-600 AD. There are 47 structures here as well as a small site museum. Bring mosquito repellant.

voyage.name: Museo Maya de Cancún and Archaeological Zone of San Miguelito
voyage.content: Museum about the Maya civilization and its many sites in the Yucatan Peninsula. Large number of artifacts from sites in and around Cancun. Next door is the San Miguelito ruins, which are partially restored and include a small pyramid.

voyage.name: Yamil Lu'um
voyage.price: Free (but may take effort to ignore touts from Westin)
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan 12.5, El Rey, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Ruins of a small Maya temple on the grounds of the Westin.

voyage.name: Punta Cancun lighthouse
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan Km. 9, Punta Cancun, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Classic red and white striped tubular lighthouse on the northern tip of the Hotel Zone.

voyage.name: El Meco Archaeological Site
voyage.content: Ruins of a Maya port from about 600 AD. El Castillo is the largest structure at the site, it is a five-level pyramid with a height of 12.5 meters and a temple at the top. A small site museum is available.

voyage.name: Torre Escénica del Embarcadero de Cancún
voyage.price: Included with cost of Xcaret ferry (show bracelet)
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan Km. 4.5, Kukulcan Boulevard, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: 80-m tower with a rotating observation deck that takes about 30 minutes for a full revolution.

voyage.name: Parque Urbano Kabah
voyage.address: Supermanzana 053 Manzana 1 L 1-01 Av. KABAH, Av. Nichupté
voyage.content: Urban ecological park with lush junglescapes and roaming wildlife including lots of friendly coatis who will gladly take that leftover burger and fries off your hands. Lots of birds, iguanas and turtles. Playgrounds for kids. Exercise equipment for adults. Hiking trails for all.

voyage.name: Palacio Municipal
voyage.content: Modern 2-story public building in a broad pedestrian square with fountains, night lights & tall trees.

voyage.name: Cancun Wax Museum
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan, La Isla, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Tourist trap wax museum that charges too much for admission then has the audacity to tell visitors they can't take pictures.

voyage.name: Museo del Automóvil Antiguo del Sureste
voyage.address: Av. Puerto Juárez entre Calle 89, Mza 116, Lote 14 16
voyage.content: Private automobile collection with lots of well-restored muscle cars.

voyage.name: Skywheel Cancun
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan km 12.5, La Isla, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: 3 turns in an air-conditioned gondola.

voyage.name: Ventura Park
voyage.content: Amusement and water park with many attractions.

voyage.name: Captain Hook Cancun
voyage.content: Shows and dinner on a pirate boat.

voyage.name: Xoximilco
voyage.content: A theme park, which is built around the culture of Mexico, food, music and customs in the Mayan jungle. It's on the highway, so easily accessible with a second-class bus or colectivos.

voyage.name: Columbus Romantic Dinner Cancun
voyage.content: Take a trip out on the calm lagoon on a beautiful boat. Steak and lobster is cooked on the boat.

voyage.name: Cancún Yachts Club
voyage.content: Yacht rentals for rental tours in all areas of Cancún, snorkeling, diving, swimming the most save water activities in yacht.

voyage.name: Punta Este Marina
voyage.content: Drive your own boat through the lagoon in the Jungle Tour and snorkel on the reef. Diving lessons and dive trips to the best dive spots in Cancún such as underwater museum.

voyage.name: Marina Aquatours
voyage.content: Exciting water tour. Choose either a jet ski or two person jet boat for a trip through the lagoon out to snorkel on the reef. Popular tours are the Jungle Tour and the Sailing Quest (Catamarans).

voyage.name: Off Road Games Cancun
voyage.content: Off-road ATV adventures.

voyage.name: Charter Fishing Cancun
voyage.content: Private and shared deep-sea fishing trips from Cancun and Isla Mujeres. Includes gear, drinks, licenses, and professional crew.

voyage.name: Cancun Fishing By Kianah
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan Km. 5.8, Kukulcan Boulevard, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Charter fishing trips starting at US$680 for 4 hours, including bait, tackle, snacks, drinks.

voyage.name: Shared Fishing Cancun
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulkan 6 (km 6 of Cancun Hotel Zone)
voyage.content: Shared deep-sea fishing trips (6 hours). Join other travelers and share the cost of the boat. Includes beers, soft drinks, ice, bait, fishing licenses, and professional crew. The dock fee of US$15 per person is not included.

voyage.name: El Tinto Golf Course
voyage.content: 18-hole jungle course that's well maintained and one of the least expensive golf courses in the region. Rental equipment and carts are a bit worn and about due for an upgrade, but for most visitors, this is one of the best options since it requires no special membership or resort affiliation.

voyage.name: Riviera Cancun
voyage.content: Modern seaside 18-hole jungle course designed by Jack Nicklaus. Holes 14 and 15 are played next to the ocean. Putting green, club house and other amenities on-site.

voyage.name: Iberostar Cancun Golf Club
voyage.content: Resort course that's a bit older, but well maintained, though the rental clubs and carts show their age. The clubhouse serves a nice breakfast if you're getting an early start. There are a couple of crocodiles living along the course, but they have eaten very few golfers lately, so leave them alone and they'll return the favor.

voyage.name: Golf Puerto Cancun
voyage.address: Av. Bonampak Lote 10, int. 1 Smza.2, Puerto Acapulco S/N, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Well kept course with a number of water and sand traps. Holes 13 and 14 are adjacent to the ocean and usually have quite a bit of wind to mess with your shots. The best time to golf is early morning when temperatures are still cool, but that's also the most popular time, so you might have to deal with crowds.

voyage.name: Playa Mujeres Golf Club
voyage.address: Prol. Bonampak, Carr. a Punta Sam s/n
voyage.content: Resort golf course with beautiful fairways but some rough conditions on the greens. Course is designed by Greg Norman and has some very difficult holes. Expect to lose lots of balls if you slice into the rough, which is mostly swamp. Good food and drink and friendly service, which includes picking you up at your hotel, if requested.

voyage.name: Pok Ta Pok
voyage.content: Natural golf course that's not well manicured with older rental equipment.

voyage.name: Moon Palace Club Golf
voyage.content: Jack Nicklaus Signature golf course with 27 holes featuring jungle and beach settings. Drinks available every 2-3 holes. Manicured fairways and greens.

voyage.name: Swim with Dolphins
voyage.content: Wet'n'Wild also offers dolphin experiences. (Beware: no cameras are allowed, they charge for the first photo and a bit less for each subsequent one). Other great places to swim with captive dolphins are Delphinus Dreams and Dolphin Discovery. Some operators offer it in the interactive aquarium of Cancún, others include a trip to Isla Mujeres, where the facilities are.

voyage.name: Always Diving
voyage.content: Scuba dive with a wide catalog of diving programs.

voyage.name: Marina Chac Chi
voyage.content: Professional PADI certified scuba diving company provides PADI Diving certifications.

voyage.name: Scuba Diving Cancun
voyage.price: Half-day dive trips start at US$69
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan KM 3.5, Kukulcan Boulevard, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: PADI certified scuba instructors. Equipment rentals. Day trips to reefs, sunken ships, and cave diving (cenotes).

voyage.name: Cancun Scuba Center
voyage.content: PADI certified dive instructors offering a variety of courses including Advanced Open Water and Divemaster as well as day trips to popular dive sites along the Great Mesoamerican Reef, Isla Mujeres, Cozumel, Cenotes and underwater rivers, etc. Offers snorkeling excursions including snorkeling with whale sharks.

voyage.name: Seatizen Divers
voyage.content: PADI and SDI diving instruction. Reef trips, cenote trips, dive trips to Undersea Museum (MUSE).

voyage.name: Manta Divers
voyage.content: Full service dive shop. PADI certified instructors and courses. Trips to MUSA (undersea museum), reefs, etc. Cenote diving available. Equipment included.

voyage.name: Scuba Total Cancun
voyage.content: A family-owned scuba diving center operating since the early 2000s. PADI-certified instructors lead small groups (maximum 4 divers).

voyage.name: Estadio Olímpico Andrés Quintana Roo
voyage.address: Av. Rodrigue Gomez y Av. Mayapan
voyage.content: Since 2020, Cancún Fútbol Club, a team in the Expansion League has played professional soccer in this small, 18,800-seat stadium in downtown. The stadium is seldom crowded.

voyage.name: Estadio Beto Avila
voyage.content: The stadium was named after former MLB and LMB player Beto Avila (known as Bobby Avila in Cleveland, where he played 10 seasons for the Indians). Cancun has had several professional baseball teams over the years, first the Marlins, then the Langosteros, and now the Tigres, who play in the Liga Mexicana de Beisbol. The Tigres play a 114-game schedule each year from late April until early September. With just under 10,

voyage.name: Market 28
voyage.content: This is a tourist-centered market in downtown Cancún, with very many souvenir shops, a central food court, and some larger Mexican restaurants. Cheaper than the hotel zone, but still considered to have 'tourist' prices, and many touts pushing for your attention. A great place if you are interested in shopping downtown and are short on time, but due to its popular and central location, prices have become more expensiv

voyage.name: Market 23
voyage.content: This is more of a 'locals' market as most products offered are like groceries, flowers, supplies, etc. Doesn't have the same range as Market 28, but is worth a visit.

voyage.name: Plaza Las Americas
voyage.content: The Plaza de las Americas offers Cinepolis (movie) Theaters, Sears, Chedraui, Liverpool and numerous smaller shops and restaurants in the mall itself and in the immediate surrounding areas not part of the mall.

voyage.name: La Isla Cancún Shopping Village
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcan km 12.5, lt 18-10, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: In the hotel zone. Features hundreds of stores ranging from American brands like Under Armour to Mexican brands like Senor Frogs. There are numerous restaurants including Chili's and McDonald's along with more local Mexican foods.

voyage.name: Kukulcan Plaza
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcan km 13, lt 410 and 411A, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Another mall down the street from 'La Isla' mall in the hotel zone featuring American and Mexican brand names such as Forever 21, GNC and Señor Frog's among other stores and restaurants.

voyage.name: Lapis Jewelry Factory
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulkan km 11.5, local 100 Int. Plaza Flamingo, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: You are likely to be offered a coupon for free jewelry at this store. Their website also offers a free gift for individuals who book a shuttle through their website. However, if you do not have any evidence of this, the offer will not be honored. A free shuttle service is offered to take you to the store from your hotel. However, the prices in the store are exorbitant (even at the "discounted" rates), and much of the

voyage.name: Ave Tulum Markets
voyage.content: There is a very large set of formal shops as well as unofficial booths that have opened up on Ave Tulum, covering a large section of the sidewalk on the west side of the road for many blocks. Souvenirs can be found for extremely cheap, and there are no aggressive shop owners hounding you to enter their store or pressuring you into buying something quickly. It would be convenient to bundle a trip here after visiting P

voyage.name: Parque de las Palapas
voyage.content: There is a good variety. The eateries are open from 10:00 and the food stalls from the evening on. All of them close around 00:00. Most places have a big sign showing the food on a picture and the according low price. Tacos as low as 30 MXN each, as of Jan 2025.

voyage.name: Food stall directly in front of the bus station
voyage.content: They have tasty tortas (sandwich) for M$25 and tacos.

voyage.name: Food stall "Tacos More"
voyage.content: Here you get well tasting tacos with fish (e.g. shrimps) for M$25 or with meat.

voyage.name: Restaurant Salus y Chemo's
voyage.content: Their red pozole and tamales is very tasty. Excellent Guerrero style food. The restaurant looks quite old which is also it’s charme.

voyage.name: Taquería el Poblano
voyage.content: Very good taqueria. Authentic Mexican food. Great portion. The waiters are very friendly. Nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: Restaurant Pipos (Bufette)
voyage.content: Very good buffet. The food with a homemade touch. Variety of dishes. The attention is very good.

voyage.name: El Cantón Toluqueño
voyage.content: There is a Comida Corrida including a soup, main dish, tortillas and drink for M$60-70. They also serves breakfast starting at M$50.

voyage.name: Fa Kee (Comida China)
voyage.content: You get a Chinese dish for M$65-80.

voyage.name: Quesadillas & sopes – Tradición Mexicana
voyage.content: As the name says, here you get quesadillas for M$18 and sopes for M$21.

voyage.name: Las Tortugas
voyage.content: Serving tortas, a kind of Mexican sandwich.

voyage.name: Atotonilco
voyage.content: An extremely good sampling of Mexican food from all around the country. Excellent value. Nothing fancy but a gastronomical delight. Try the "Huevos Motuleños".

voyage.name: Los de Pescados
voyage.content: Taco restaurant specializing in seafood. Fish tacos cost M$37 (July 2021) and are a few pieces of fried fish with some tortillas. You put your own sauces and condiments.

voyage.name: Pescaditos
voyage.content: Really nice and laid back seafood restaurant where everything's deep fried. Try the chiles rellenos, possibly the best ones in Cancún.

voyage.name: La Habichuela
voyage.content: La Habichuela is a must-visit with its Mexican cuisine, Mayan setting and Caribbean seafood. This restaurant has been open since 1977 and is a legend in Cancún. The romantic, outside garden is a popular place to dine with the decoration of various native trees and plants that create a beautiful illusion of the Mayan ruins under the night sky. La Habicheula received the National Best Restaurant Award and has been a pa

voyage.name: Café trova El Pabilo
voyage.content: Art exhibitions every 15 days. Good baguettes and wine.

voyage.name: Los Tarascos
voyage.content: Classic Mexican taqueria specializing in tacos al pastor. Very popular with the locals, quite tasty and at a fair price.

voyage.name: Cambalache
voyage.content: This Argentine steakhouse serves up one of the best menus in Cancún. The atmosphere inside the restaurant makes you feel you have travelled an extra 1000 mi. The staff's attention to detail and desire to please make you feel like you're the only one they are serving that night. Great place to have a dinner with the one you love or enjoy the company of friends. The food alone could give this place a 4-star rating, the

voyage.name: Lorenzillo's
voyage.address: Km 10.5, Blvd. Kukulcan, Punta Cancun, Zona Hotelera

voyage.name: RosaNegra
voyage.content: Latin American cuisine.

voyage.name: Mikado
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcán, Retorno Chac L-41, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Japanese and Thai cuisine featuring teppanyaki tables.

voyage.name: Champions Sports Bar
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcán, Retorno Chac L-41, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Stepped up bar food with all the games on over 40 screens.

voyage.name: Gustino
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcán, km 14.5, Lote 40-A, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Gustino has authentic Italian cuisine using the freshest Mediterranean ingredients.

voyage.name: Señor Frogs
voyage.content: Señor Frog's is a restaurant by day and a dance club by night, and is one of the most popular spots for vacationers to visit. The restaurant opens up for lunch and serves international types of food such as pasta, chicken and pizza as well as Mexican cuisine all day until midnight. A cover charge of five dollars will get you into the party after 20:00 and includes a souvenir yard glass which you can then pay to get f

voyage.name: Dady'O
voyage.content: Dady'O has been known to host some of the world's top DJs, including Red Foo (LMFAO), Apl.De.App and Tiësto, features a casual atmosphere, laser shows, pole dancing go go girls and flashing dance floor opening shows.

voyage.name: Coco Bongo
voyage.content: A nightclub featuring a show that has been compared with Las Vegas. More than 50 professionals in scenery. Tickets can be bought online for US$75. If you don't mind waiting to get in exchangeable tickets can be bought from Oxxo for M$1000.

voyage.name: La Vaquita
voyage.content: Loud, open front party bar in the heart of the Hotel Zone. You can't miss the cow print decor or the booming bass of the non-stop party. Known for innovative drinks and a lively crowd.

voyage.name: Surfin' Burrito
voyage.address: Kukulkan Km. 9.5, Punta Cancun, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Liter-size margaritas, buckets of beer, and spicy micheladas. The house favorite is the Coco Loco, coconut juice and rum served in a coconut shell. Food options include shrimp tacos and coconut shrimp.

voyage.name: Los 4 Elementos
voyage.content: Try the live music bar Los 4 Elementos. They open and play live music from 23:00 until the last customer leaves. The music is great and prices are significantly lower than those found in the hotel zone clubs.

voyage.name: Route 666 Biker Bar
voyage.content: Lively club serving beer in buckets (cubetas) with casual food like wings, fries and burgers. Live music with a lot of rock and metal bands played at loud volumes. Fun place.

voyage.name: 11:11 Club
voyage.address: Av Tulum Smz 22 Mz 5 Lote 33, Centro
voyage.content: Lively atmosphere, drag performers, live music and DJs, plus great mixed drinks.

voyage.name: Laser Hot Beer & Queer
voyage.content: Fun atmosphere, drag queen cabaret with live music or DJs, beers and large mixed drinks.

voyage.name: Puerto Juarez Brewery
voyage.content: Super small craft brewery with a range of ales from a light golden ale, a Belgian strong, a brown ale flavored with chilis, and of course, the always ubiquitous IPA. Light food includes seafood, tacos and a nice charcuterie board with sliced sausages and cheese.

voyage.name: Hotel Rivemar
voyage.content: In the downtown area near the bus station. Front desk help is very friendly. You can keep your bags at the hotel even after checking out. You can take the Rt. 1 bus to the hotel/beaches district. When booking directly at the hotel it's M$650 for 1 person and M$750 for 2 persons. (April 2022)

voyage.name: Fiesta Party Hostel - Cancun
voyage.content: This hostel does not fail to live up to its name, and if you are looking to hang out with your fellow party people, you shouldn't be disappointed here, where drinks and revelry flow freely. If you don't like noise, on the other hand, this might not be the most ideal accommodation. But the establishment does provide free breakfast and dinner plus bus trips to the beach and a happy hour every evening.

voyage.name: Mayan Monkey Hostel & Bar
voyage.price: A dorm costs around M$600 (April 2022) including taxes

voyage.name: Selina Cancun Laguna Hotel Zone & Cowork
voyage.price: A bed in a dorm is around M$460 (April 2022)

voyage.name: The Yellow Capsule
voyage.content: If you missed the chance to stay at a capsule hotel in Japan, you can do it right here in Cancun. The spaceship-like compartments and interiors are clean, and the complimentary breakfast includes an egg sandwich. Plus, the lodging has airport shuttles and organized tours to places such as Isla Mujeres.

voyage.name: Temptation Resort and Spa
voyage.content: 2-3 star with 3 restaurants. Reservations to be made from 10:00-11:00 the previous day. Beach front is calm mainly for boat use.

voyage.name: Parador Hotel
voyage.address: Ave Tulum N°26, SM 5, MZA 5, Lote 1, Col Centro
voyage.content: A/C, cableTV, and internet connection. Swimming pool, fitness room/gym, and a restaurant, bar, and café.

voyage.name: Crown Paradise Club
voyage.content: Features a water park for the kids with a pirate ship and 8 water slides, à la carte and buffet dining, adult only areas, mini golf, disco, nightly entertainment.

voyage.name: Grand Oasis Cancún
voyage.address: Boulevard Kukulcan Km 16.5 Lt45-47, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Resort with a college-aged crowd. The rooms are clean and surprisingly spacious for the price. The pool is generally crowded during peak times but is large and features several swim-up bars. The bad part is that since the Oasis is all-inclusive you basically get what you pay for, the food and drinks are not the best quality. The buffet-style restaurants are bland and the food can get quite repetitive. An exception is

voyage.name: RIU Cancún
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcan km 8.5, Manzana 50, Lote 5, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Resort with views of the Caribbean Sea. Several restaurants and bars. Choice of activities and entertainment options, including a sports bar, night club and theatre with theme shows.

voyage.name: RIU Caribe
voyage.content: All inclusive resort with Mayan-style architecture overlooking the Caribbean. 506 sea view rooms with mini-bar and liquor dispenser. Several restaurants, bars and facilities including 24-hr snacks and beverages. Fun and relaxing atmosphere created by the large swimming pool and spectacular beach.

voyage.name: The Royal Resorts
voyage.content: The Royal Resorts have been around since 1974 and include a string of 4 hotels all in close vicinity of each other. The Royal Mayan, The Royal Caribbean and The Royal Islander are side by side whereas the newest hotel, The Royal Sands, is no more than a five minute ride by bus. The Royal Resorts offer beautiful villas that overlook the Gulf of Mexico. Each villa is equipped with a kitchen, two bathrooms, two bedrooms

voyage.name: Sandos Cancun
voyage.address: Retorno del Rey km 14, Mz 53, Lt 37-1
voyage.content: The Sandos Cancun is called the jewel of the Sandos Resort chain. They are a 4-diamond AAA rated all inclusive resort. The resort is themed and offers unique entertainment called the Rhythm Experience. Sandos has a vacation club called Royal Elite that sells a timeshare-like membership. Membership affords special amenities like private access to bars including top shelf liquors, first access to restaurants and access

voyage.name: Soberanis Hotel
voyage.content: The rooms are all air-conditioned. They have cable television, a private toilet and bath, and safe. the rooms are further equipped with an IDD telephone, internet access, and a writing desk and chair. Rates include daily breakfast. Non-smoking rooms are available.

voyage.name: Sotavento Hotel and Yacht Club
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan km 4 Zona Hotelera, Calle del Pescador, Lote D-8-4
voyage.content: In front of Nichupte Laguna and is within walking distance to sandy beaches and downtown area. Internet and cable TV. Non-smoking rooms can be requested.

voyage.name: GR Solaris Caribe
voyage.address: Blvd. Kukulcan km 20.5, lt 64 bis 2da etapa Sección A, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Adults-Only All Inclusive Resort.

voyage.name: Beach Palace Cancun
voyage.address: Beach Palace Cancún Boulevard Kukulcan Km 11.5, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Family hotel.

voyage.name: CasaMagna Marriott Cancún Resort
voyage.content: 418 rooms and 34 suites. Each room has a private balcony with a table and chairs. 3 restaurants on-site, including a steakhouse, a Japanese restaurant and a sports bar. The hotel tends to be priced on the higher side for Cancún, but that also tends to weed out the younger crowd. This resort is adjacent to the JW Marriott Cancún and is directly connected to it through a pathway. There are up-charges for almost everyth

voyage.name: Casa Turquesa Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: 29-suite boutique hotel has amenities including an infinity pool with swim up bar, spa, two restaurants and an onsite art gallery. Suites have 32” flat screen satellite TV, minibar and full bathrooms with separate bathtub and shower. Jacuzzi on the terrace/balcony. Airport transportation can be arranged. Rates depend upon room category/season.

voyage.name: ClubMed
voyage.content: An all inclusive resort. A short distance outside the town, at the tip of the bay. The Caribbean Sea is on one side and on the other is a lagoon. Club Med was the first to establish itself here around 30 years ago. Traditional central square, bungalow-haciendas and speciality restaurants.

voyage.name: Hyatt Ziva Cancún
voyage.alt: formerly Dreams Cancún Resort and Spa
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcan Manzana 51 LT7, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: Surrounded by the sea on 3 sides. All-inclusive resort catering to families. All rooms have private balcony views of the ocean, beaches, lagoon or gardens. Marble floors, dining area, mini-bar, satellite TV and 24 hr room service. Several have private whirlpools. A pod of 6 dolphins is held in the resorts lagoon. Swims with the captive dolphins programs are available for guests and the general public.

voyage.name: All Ritmo Cancun Resort & Waterpark
voyage.address: Carretera a Puerto Juárez-Punta Sam km 1.5 lt 128
voyage.content: Family hotel offers activities for children and events for adults.

voyage.name: Fiesta Americana Grand Coral Beach Cancún Resort & Spa
voyage.content: AAA 5-diamond resort has 602 rooms. The hotel is outwardly hostile toward same-sex couples. 5 restaurants, one of which is the Le Basilic restaurant is one of only three 5-diamond restaurants found in Mexico. 4 bars, a spa, fitness and business center, a very long swimming pool, and a sun deck.

voyage.name: Paradisus Cancún
voyage.content: Well known for its white sandy beach overlooking the Caribbean Sea. 4 pools, specialized à la carte restaurants, and activities program for children and adults. 9 hole, par three golf course, a tennis court, 2 paddle tennis courts and has received an award from The Leading Hotels of the World as a Leading Spa of the World.

voyage.name: Iberostar Selection Cancún
voyage.content: The only golf & spa resort on the island is an Iberostar all-inclusive. 426 ocean-view rooms, including 82 villas with a private lounge and executive services; 5 restaurants, including a gourmet-dining beachside grill and swim up bar; 7 infinity pools and the largest beach in Cancún. If you are having trouble with the local food, try the hotel's club sandwich.

voyage.name: Grand Park Royal Cancún
voyage.content: 5-star hotel with 296 rooms and views of the Caribbean.

voyage.name: Krystal Grand Cancun
voyage.content: 5-star hotel with a seafront location. 295 rooms.

voyage.name: JW Marriott Cancún Resort
voyage.content: Adjacent to the CasaMagna Marriott Cancún Resort and has a connected pathway. 448 rooms with private balconies and views of the Caribbean. Mayan-inspired spa, 4 world-class restaurants and over of meeting space. Caters to Mexican weddings, events and conferences.

voyage.name: Live Aqua Cancún
voyage.content: 371 deluxe rooms, including 36 suites. The modern design is stunning. The service is a close second but the rooms are small. 3 restaurants, including one by celebrity chef Michelle Bernstein, 1 by chef Franco Maddalozzo, and a Mexican restaurant. There is also a wine and mescal bar. 8 pools which vary in temperature and 12 spa treatment rooms. The hotel is reserved for adults.

voyage.name: Marriott Amar House
voyage.content: Rooms offer views, custom art and furnishings by artist Yuri Zatarain, monsoon showers and Aveda bath amenities.

voyage.name: Omni Cancún Hotel & Villas
voyage.content: 5-star resort between the Caribbean and Nichupte Lagoon on Cancún Island. 341 guest rooms and villas with full service spa.

voyage.name: Now Sapphire Riviera Cancun
voyage.address: Mz 9, Lt 10 y 11, Zona Federal Maritima, Puerto Morelos
voyage.content: All-inclusive resort stretches along a lush tropical mangrove preserve on a 5,000 ft long Caribbean coastline.

voyage.name: Kempinski Hotel Cancun
voyage.content: 5-star beachfront resort hotel with luxuriously appointed rooms and suites, a large beachfront outdoor swimming pool with available cabanas, 4 on-site restaurants and 2 bars. Spa services available.

voyage.name: Riu Palace Las Americas
voyage.address: Blvd Kukulcan km 8.5, Mz 50, Lt 4, Zona Hotelera
voyage.content: 372 suites, ocean views, and all-inclusive dining, beverages and entertainment.

voyage.content: 90 suites, all have balcony or deck with ocean views, daily serving of champagne and fresh fruit, complimentary unlimited calls worldwide, welcome bottle of tequila and handmade beach bag. Hydrothalasoo pool and aqua gym, spa with private massage cabins and jacuzzi, and chauffeured airport transfer. This property is located in Puerto Morelos, 32-48 km (20-30) miles south of Cancun.

voyage.content: Resort features villas with washer/dryer, dishwasher, full kitchen, living room, dining room, jetted tub. The property has two infinity pools.
